title: review: fix round: watchdog review findings (uv --project restart, test registry isolation, mcp-hosted daemon liveness, pid reuse, per-repo isolation)
spec:
Fix round for the watchdog (T-1679/T-1682) after an independent full-diff security review (Planner-run,
2026-10-06, REQUEST_CHANGES). Work in /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/wt/T-1682 on branch task/T-1682 (head a8a5909); add
commits on top. Fix all of these:

H1 watchdog.py:179 restart runs `uv run orchestrator daemon` in the target repo without --project; installed repos run
   the orchestrator via `uv run --project <orchestrator repo>` (install.py:66), so restarts fail ("Failed to spawn:
   orchestrator") or run a target repo's own script. Use [uv, "run", "--project", <orchestrator package repo root>,
   "orchestrator", "daemon"] with ORCH_ROOT=<repo>, like install.py.
H2 daemon.acquire_lock registers every repo, and tests/_harness.py never sets ORCH_MACHINE_DIR, so test_daemon's
   Background tests (test_daemon.py ~3672-3682) wrote temp fixture repos into the real ~/.orchestrator-machine/repos.json.
   (a) tests/_harness.py sets ORCH_MACHINE_DIR to a temp dir before any orchestrator import; (b) machine.register_repo and
   the watchdog accept only real installs: <path>/.orchestrator/pool.toml exists and the path is not under
   tempfile.gettempdir() or /private/var/folders; entries failing this are ignored (pruned from repos.json by the watchdog
   run, which is the watchdog's own state file). Add tests for both.
H3 watchdog.py:76 liveness requires "daemon" in the ps command, but with [daemon].autostart the daemon runs as a thread in
   `python -m orchestrator.mcp`, whose pid is in daemon.lock (daemon.py ~1962, ~2035) -> false "dead" every pass, extra
   daemon starts, a log file every 5 min, false alerts. Write a marker into the lock: "<pid> <kind> <process start time>"
   (kind = cli or mcp; start time from `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` or psutil-free equivalent) and accept both kinds.
M4 liveness by substring lets a reused pid pass (claude -p workers have orchestrator paths and the word daemon in argv; a
   daemon of another repo also passes). Compare the stored process start time with the live one and check the process
   is a python running orchestrator (cli daemon or orchestrator.mcp) with ORCH_ROOT or cwd equal to the repo where
   determinable; mismatch = dead.
M5 watchdog.py:224-226 and :45/:73/:98/:130/:206: one bad repo aborts the pass for all. Wrap each repo in try/except in
   run_once (log one line, continue); bound/validate the pid (positive int < 2**31, catch OverflowError/ValueError);
   type-check task fields (status str, depends_on list of str, id str); tolerate files vanishing between glob and stat.
M6 watchdog.py:14 bare "spawn" marker matches routine reasons ("re-spawned after account B cooldown", "respawn path").
   Match only specific markers: "claude CLI not found", "not found on PATH", "no_cli", "launch_error".
L7 claude_cli.py:14 discard non-absolute results of shutil.which.
L8 watchdog.py:285-298 escape paths in the printed plist with xml.sax.saxutils.escape.
Tests for each item in tests/test_watchdog.py (and the harness change), all with temp machine dirs. Do not touch the
real ~/.orchestrator-machine. Run in the foreground: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_watchdog
tests.test_spawn tests.test_daemon (pytest may be missing). Commit on task/T-1682.
acceptance: each of H1-H3, M4-M6, L7-L8 is fixed and has a named test in tests/test_watchdog.py
tests/_harness.py sets ORCH_MACHINE_DIR to a temp dir; the test suite leaves ~/.orchestrator-machine untouched
tests.test_watchdog, tests.test_spawn and tests.test_daemon pass (the two pre-existing merge-base errors excepted)

result.summary: H1-H3, M4-M6 and L7-L8 are each fixed in the diff and each has a named test in tests/test_watchdog.py. The harness now sets ORCH_MACHINE_DIR to a temp dir. The gate was green on the first attempt. I did not run the suites myself. Two low-severity risks are noted.

comments.issue: _process_root falls back to the process cwd when ORCH_ROOT is not in the environment. An mcp-hosted daemon whose cwd is not the repo root (for example a subdirectory or worktree) is then reported dead. The result is a repeated restart attempt that cannot take the lock, plus a false alert.
is_daemon_command splits the command line on whitespace. An interpreter or script path that contains spaces breaks the python-basename and name checks, so a live daemon is reported dead.
